episodes.201520: A weak upper disturbance crossed the area ahead of a cold front touching off a few severe thunderstorms.
episodes.201532: An upper low moved across the desert southwest June 1st into June 2nd helping to pull up higher moisture from former Tropical Storm Alvin in the eastern Pacific. Widespread showers and storms developed across New Mexico during the day June 2nd as the upper low moved into the state. Storms resulted in severe wind gusts in Clovis, penny size hail and flash flooding in Albuquerque and Farmington. Flash flooding in the north diversion arroyo channel in east central Albuquerque resulted in a fatality. Storms across the state tapered off after sunset with the loss of daytime heating and the system exiting east of the state. A 2nd upper low approached the state on June 3rd resulting in the diurnal development of storms across the Four Corners area. Storms brought quarter size hail and flash flooding to the Farmington area. ||Another round of showers and storms developed across western NM on June 4th as the upper low entered the state. These storms moved east across the state bringing flash flooding and large hail to parts of the middle Rio Grande Valley and east central New Mexico during the afternoon and evening hours before exiting into the Texas Panhandle just before midnight. More rounds of severe storms developed along the dryline across far eastern New Mexico during the late afternoon and evening hours of June 5th and 6th. These storms brought large hail 1 to 2 inches in diameter to Curry and Roosevelt Counties both days and western Union County on June 6th. Additionally, several brief tornadoes were observed across east central and southeast Roosevelt County on June 5th.||Key Impacts: Hail, Flash Flood, Tornado, Severe Thunderstorm Wind Gust.
episodes.201939: Scattered thunderstorms developed on the afternoon of the second producing severe wind gusts across the South Plains and extreme southern Texas Panhandle. A strong short wave trough moved across southern Arizona into New Mexico bringing robust large scale ascent to West Texas. Very strong surface heating with temperatures warming into the 90s created a deeply mixed boundary layer. Thunderstorms developed early in the afternoon with a quick erosion of a cap, however, the warm surface temperatures kept cloud bases very high. As a result, numerous severe outflow winds were observed from this thunderstorm activity. Several locations around the South Plains incurred damage from the intense winds.
episodes.201968: A strong cold front pushed across Wyoming and into the high plains the evening of June 2nd. Scattered thunderstorms developed ahead and near the cold front and moved east and southeast into western Nebraska. Large hail and strong damaging winds were reported with these thunderstorms.
episodes.201970: Severe thunderstorms pushing east out of eastern Wyoming moved into western Nebraska during the evening of June 2nd. These storms continued to produce large hail and strong damaging winds.
episodes.202628: An incoming trough, upslope flow, and a somewhat weak dryline resulted in the development of scattered thunderstorms across Southeast New Mexico and West Texas. A few of these storms became severe, producing damaging winds and large hail. The two most notable storms occurred in Fort Stockton and Pleasant Farms. Microbursts in these locations resulted in winds in excess of 100 mph and widespread damage to roofs and mobile homes. Two people were injured in Pleasant Farms.
episodes.202630: An incoming trough, upslope flow, and a somewhat weak dryline resulted in the development of scattered thunderstorms across Southeast New Mexico and West Texas. A few of these storms became severe, producing damaging winds and large hail. The two most notable storms occurred in Fort Stockton and Pleasant Farms. Microbursts in these locations resulted in winds in excess of 100 mph and widespread damage to roofs and mobile homes. Two people were injured in Pleasant Farms.
episodes.202642: During the early afternoon of June 2nd, scattered storms developed over parts of eastern New Mexico and the far southwestern Texas Panhandle. These storms quickly grew in coverage expanding northward into a line before moving easterly across the combined Oklahoma and Texas Panhandles. Some of these storms were severe with the main impact being damaging wind gusts.
episodes.202643: During the early afternoon of June 2nd, scattered storms developed over parts of eastern New Mexico and the far southwestern Texas Panhandle. These storms quickly grew in coverage expanding northward into a line before moving easterly across the combined Oklahoma and Texas Panhandles. Some of these storms were severe with the main impact being damaging wind gusts.
episodes.202671: Scattered severe thunderstorms impacted portions of western and northern Oklahoma on the afternoon and evening of the 2nd. The combination of strong instability and sufficient wind shear (aided by the passage of a weak shortwave trough) promoted organized thunderstorms. A few reports of large hail and thunderstorm wind damage were received across the aforementioned areas.
episodes.202699: Remnant moisture plume from a tropical system with precipitable water values between 1.0-1.4, which for early June is near record levels, combined with a series of low pressure systems that affected the Desert Southwest to result in periods of showers and thunderstorms between June 1-4. The first round of rainfall activity was observed across south-central AZ during the overnight hours of June 1-2, with observed amounts of 1-2 inches across northern portions of the Phoenix area towards the foothills and higher terrain areas to the north and east. The rainfall was enough to result in flood impacts near the Wildcat Burn Scar located east of Carefree. Another round of rainfall activity was observed during the overnight hours of June 3-4 across portions of La Paz County in association with a secondary low pressure system that resulted in a road closure near Parker due to flooding.
episodes.202789: Showers and thunderstorms brought gusty outflow winds.
episodes.203037: In the late afternoon of the 2nd, a cluster of storms formed in far western Kansas and proceeded to the north-northeast. Across western Kansas, these storms produced winds up to 80 MPH and penny sized hail. The strongest winds were associated with an outflow boundary coming from the cluster that also produced a haboob (wall of dust) that reduced visibility down to zero. This was a unique system because the overall system and wall of dust generally moved from south to north.  A short landspout tornado occurred ahead of the wall of dust in Sherman County.
episodes.203193: On the afternoon of June 1st, an outflow boundary from morning thunderstorms, combined with a strong shortwave trough moving south from the Southern Plains into North Texas, created a focus for thunderstorm development. These storms began near the I-20 corridor and moved south throughout the afternoon, eventually dissipating over Central Texas by evening. The most significant severe weather event associated with this system was large hail, up to 3, in Parker and Tarrant counties.
episodes.203290: An approaching cold front and upper level disturbance, initiated thunderstorms over northern Custer County during the late afternoon hours of June 2nd. This activity then developed along a line from northern Lincoln into southeastern Holt County. This activity tracked slowly to the south into southwestern and central Nebraska and continued into the overnight hours. Heavy rain produced flash flooding in northern Custer County. Large hail up to golf ball size and wind gusts to 70 MPH were reported with the strongest storms.
episodes.203537: A complex of showers and thunderstorms moved across northeastern Minnesota during the afternoon hours of the 2nd. While most of the storms were sub severe, a dying storm near Grand Rapids was able to produce some gusty winds that toppled a few birch trees across US Highway 2.
episodes.203595: Multiple severe hail reports and a severe wind gust reported with morning thunderstorms associated with a stalled surface frontal boundary across the central Florida peninsula.
episodes.203596: Morning thunderstorms associated with a stalled surface frontal boundary across the central Florida peninsula produce gusty winds across the Tampa Bay and Charlotte Harbor area waters.
episodes.203605: Severe thunderstorms produced severe wind gusts over parts of west central Minnesota.
episodes.203706: An upper-level trough entered SW Kansas providing enough lift and moisture for thunderstorm development. As the storms progressed and strengthened, they established a cold pool and congealed into a line of storms producing severe wind gusts.
episodes.203790: A cold front swept across western and central Wyoming and brought severe thunderstorms to Yellowstone National Park.
episodes.204088: A line of storms produced widespread wind damage and isolated hail up to 1.25 inches in diameter during the afternoon and early evening of Monday, June 2nd. Much of the damage came from downed trees or power lines. The highest measured wind gust was recorded by a MNDOT RWIS site along Highway 9 east of Benson at 78 mph.
episodes.204278: Broad wave was in place over the area, allowing for high based thunderstorms to develop across the far southeastern plains.
episodes.204317: An anomalous early push of tropical moisture from the remnants of Tropical Storm Alvin brought strong thunderstorms and heavy rainfall to Southeast Arizona. Notably, there was damage to electrical equipment in Douglas, AZ causing a power outage to 1,400 people.
episodes.204838: Scattered gale-force wind gusts occurred in association with thunderstorms that developed over the Upper Florida Keys and adjacent coastal waters.  These thunderstorms were well south of a stationary frontal boundary positioned across the central Florida peninsula, as the western portion of a ridge across the western north Atlantic moved northward.
episodes.204922: Scattered strong to severe thunderstorms developed late afternoon along a slow-moving frontal boundary. Even with fairly weak deep-layer shear, strong instability resulted in large hail. Drier air and advancing cold pools later in development produced spotty damaging winds. High moisture content and slowly progressing storms also produced some locally heavy rainfall with rates briefly from 3 to 5 inches per hour.||A particularly intense and long-lived supercell developed near Vermillion and tracked southeast, generating hail up to golf ball size and a swath of damaging winds along Burbank Road up to 85 mph.
episodes.204939: Scattered strong to severe thunderstorms developed late afternoon along a slow-moving frontal boundary. Even with fairly weak deep-layer shear, strong instability resulted in large hail. Drier air and advancing cold pools later in development produced spotty damaging winds. High moisture content and slowly progressing storms also produced some locally heavy rainfall with rates briefly from 3 to 5 inches per hour.
episodes.204941: Scattered strong to severe thunderstorms developed late afternoon along a slow-moving frontal boundary. Even with fairly weak deep-layer shear, strong instability resulted in large hail. Drier air and advancing cold pools later in development produced spotty damaging winds. High moisture content and slowly progressing storms also produced some locally heavy rainfall with rates briefly from 3 to 5 inches per hour.
episodes.204942: Scattered strong to severe thunderstorms developed late afternoon along a slow-moving frontal boundary. Even with fairly weak deep-layer shear, strong instability resulted in large hail. Drier air and advancing cold pools later in development produced spotty damaging winds. High moisture content and slowly progressing storms also produced some torrential rainfall with rates briefly from 3 to 5 inches per hour.||One particularly intense supercell developed near Vermillion, South Dakota and moved southeast through early evening, producing large hail, damaging wind, and heavy rainfall just over the Missouri River into northeast Nebraska before weakening.
episodes.205092: Strong to severe thunderstorms developed along the Atlantic coast of southeastern Florida on the afternoon of June 2.
